parsed.claim: Confirmed IDOR on GET /api/v2/orders/{id} — endpoint authenticates session but does not check resource ownership. Reproducible across 5 distinct order IDs with evidence chain: credential verification (GET /api/me), DB ownership proof (SELECT query), auth boundary test (401 without session), and differential control (authenticated user accessing own order vs. other user's order).
coverage_gaps: Parameter pollution / alternative HTTP methods (POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS) not tested for same vulnerability
Batch enumeration breadth unconfirmed—only 5 discrete order_ids tested; claim of 'affects ALL orders' not quantified across larger range (e.g., IDs 1-1000)
Response content scope underspecified—evidence confirms user_id=2 disclosure, but scope of sensitive field leakage (payment method, shipping address, etc.) not detailed
parsed.deception_check: The operator may be reading the 401 boundary check generously—correct rejection of unauthenticated access does not validate authorization for authenticated requests; however, the core evidence (user A reading user B's order) is direct and avoids this pitfall.

objections.concern: Evidence files referenced but not provided in this critique—summary is credible but unvalidated against raw HTTP request/response pairs
objections.evidence_request: Provide actual HTTP files (request-1.http through request-5.http, response-1.http through response-5.http) to verify cookie/session tokens are distinct per user and responses contain full order data

objections.concern: PATCH write vulnerability mentioned but scoped separately—unclear if PATCH has additional protections (CSRF token, re-auth, signature requirement) that would affect the overall authorization failure assessment
objections.evidence_request: Clarify whether PATCH vulnerability operates under identical authorization absence or has different constraints

objections.concern: Happy-path authorization not explicitly stated—whether user A can successfully access their own orders (baseline control) confirmed
objections.evidence_request: Confirm that GET /api/v2/orders/{user_a_order_id} with user A's session returns 200 and correct user_id=1 in response body

parsed.one_more_thread: Test batch enumeration across a wider order_id range (e.g., sequential IDs 1-1000, or sample across magnitude) to characterize full blast radius and identify whether access is truly universal or constrained (e.g., time-based, range-constrained); test parameter pollution via POST body with `order_id` or alternative parameter names to rule out method-specific authorization; obtain and review authorization middleware code to determine whether the check is entirely absent or misconfigured (e.g., role check backwards, user_id check skipped due to refactor)."
